From d1883cefd31752f0504b94c3bcfa1f6d511d6e87 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Hans de Goede <johannes.goede@oss.qualcomm.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2025 17:37:27 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] leds: led-class: Only Add LED to leds_list when it is fully
 ready

Before this change the LED was added to leds_list before led_init_core()
gets called adding it the list before led_classdev.set_brightness_work gets
initialized.

This leaves a window where led_trigger_register() of a LED's default
trigger will call led_trigger_set() which calls led_set_brightness()
which in turn will end up queueing the *uninitialized*
led_classdev.set_brightness_work.

This race gets hit by the lenovo-thinkpad-t14s EC driver which registers
2 LEDs with a default trigger provided by snd_ctl_led.ko in quick
succession. The first led_classdev_register() causes an async modprobe of
snd_ctl_led to run and that async modprobe manages to exactly hit
the window where the second LED is on the leds_list without led_init_core()
being called for it, resulting in:

 
diff --git a/drivers/leds/led-class.c b/drivers/leds/led-class.c
index 885399ed0776..d34a19453560 100644
--- a/drivers/leds/led-class.c
+++ b/drivers/leds/led-class.c
@@ -560,11 +560,6 @@ int led_classdev_register_ext(struct device *parent,
 #ifdef CONFIG_LEDS_BRIGHTNESS_HW_CHANGED
 	led_cdev->brightness_hw_changed = -1;
 #endif
-	/* add to the list of leds */
-	down_write(&leds_list_lock);
-	list_add_tail(&led_cdev->node, &leds_list);
-	up_write(&leds_list_lock);
-
 	if (!led_cdev->max_brightness)
 		led_cdev->max_brightness = LED_FULL;
 
@@ -574,6 +569,11 @@ int led_classdev_register_ext(struct device *parent,
 
 	led_init_core(led_cdev);
 
+	/* add to the list of leds */
+	down_write(&leds_list_lock);
+	list_add_tail(&led_cdev->node, &leds_list);
+	up_write(&leds_list_lock);
+
 #ifdef CONFIG_LEDS_TRIGGERS
 	led_trigger_set_default(led_cdev);
 #endif
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

The patch modifies a single file: **drivers/leds/led-class.c**. It corrects the order of initialization steps in the `led_classdev_register_ext()` function to prevent a race condition.

### Modifications in `drivers/leds/led-class.c`
- **Removed** the block that adds the LED to the `leds_list` (via `list_add_tail`) from its original position, which was **before** `led_init_core(led_cdev)`.
- **Added** the same block **after** `led_init_core(led_cdev)` and **before** the call to `led_trigger_set_default(led_cdev)`.

### Relationship
The change ensures that when a default trigger is set (which may immediately try to set brightness and schedule the `set_brightness_work`), the LED's internal core data structures – specifically the `set_brightness_work` work queue – are already fully initialized. Previously, adding the LED to the global list before `led_init_core()` exposed a window where an asynchronous trigger registration could access an uninitialized work queue, causing a crash. By delaying the list addition until after `led_init_core()`, the LED is only visible to other subsystems when it is in a fully operational state.
